text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 2440 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- Pope John Paul II arrives in Hungary today for a two-day visit during which he will mark the 1,000-year anniversary of the abbey of Pannonhalma and celebrate a huge outdoor mass in Gyor.
- The restored synagogue in Budapest was ceremoniously inaugurated on Thursday.

- The cabinet announced that an Information Science and Technology Innovation Park would be erected. The government decided that it will submit to Parliament an amendment to the bill on the service of professional soldiers in the armed forces.
- US Congressman Tom Lantos on an official visit to Hungary was received by President Arpad Goncz and twice by Prime Minister Gyula Horn.
- Gyorgy Radnai, chairman of the Voluntary Mutual Insurance Funds Supervision Authority, said the security of members demands the establishment of guaranty funds.
- Acel Kft, a company owned by the management of the giant steel industry holding Dunaferr has won a tender to manage Dunaferr's assets.
- Some 10,000 to 20,000 people demonstrated against the Hungarian-Romanian basic treaty in Kossuth square outside Parliament.
NEPSZABADSAG
- The Hungarian Socialist Party will be declared a full member of the Socialist International at the 20th congress of the organisation starting in New York next Monday.
- The first draft of the supplementary budget, which concerns the use of HUF 40 billion in public money, has just been completed.
NEPSZAVA
- German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said that a DM 500 million loan agreement for Hungary is expected to be signed when Prime Minister Gyula Horn visits his country on October 3.
MAGYAR NEMZET
- President Arpad Goncz and Prime Minister Gyula Horn Thursday separately received former Israeli Prime Minister Yitzhak Shamir.
MAGYAR HIRLAP

- A one-round open tender will be announced for the sale of the state's 90 per cent stake in Recsk Ore Mines with a face value of HUF 8 billion and for another one-round open tender for a 76 per cent stake in the liquor factory Gyori Likorgyar.
- A consortium of GE Capital and France's Alsthom-Delas has won a HUF 4.8 billion tender called by the nuclear power plant Paks Atomeromu to replace the condensors.
- Budapest Bank achieved a first-half gross profit of HUF 3.5 billion and a balance sheet footing of HUF 212.5 billion.

- Creditanstalt Rt, the fully owned subsidiary of Creditanstalt Bankverein Austria, saw its gross profit exceed HUF 2 billion and its balance sheet footing rise by 37 per cent to HUF 106 billion through the first eight months of the year.
- The State Privatisation and Holding Co. closed July with a surpluse of HUF 12.5 billion, up from the HUF 10.7 billion deficit it registered at the end of the first half.
- The world's largest mobile exhibition hall, owned by the Dutch electronics company Philips, is now on display in Budapest.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- The Hungarian airline Malev Rt. has proposed to foreign airlines in Hungary that official fares be raised by an average 10 per cent.
-- Budapest newsroom (36-1) 266 2410
